section_summary: This section centers on Japan’s completion of the reconstruction of Tokyo and Yokohama after the 1923 Great Kantō Earthquake and on the 1930 visit to the United States of the Jiji Shimpo’s women “Envoys of Gratitude.” It documents the envoys’ selection, biographies, itinerary, official courtesies, meetings with President and Mrs. Hoover, and messages thanking the American government, the Red Cross, and the public for earthquake relief. The section also contains correspondence about a 1935 memorial service for earthquake victims and 1936 cross-references concerning publication of the historical correspondence.

subfiles.title: Japanese note announcing completion of Tokyo’s reconstruction
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Announces the completion of Tokyo’s post-earthquake reconstruction and thanks the United States for its relief and support.
subfiles.summary: Japan reports Tokyo's reconstruction after the 1923 earthquake complete, celebrates March 26, and thanks the American government and people for sympathy, relief and cooperation.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to the Japanese reconstruction note
subfiles.from: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japan’s thanks for American assistance after the 1923 earthquake.
subfiles.summary: Cotton acknowledges Debuchi’s notice that Tokyo’s reconstruction has been completed and his government’s expression of appreciation. He characterizes the American response to the disaster as a spontaneous and sincere manifestation of the cordial friendship between the two countries.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on reimbursement for a memorial wreath
subfiles.about: Recommends reimbursement of Edwin L. Neville for a wreath sent to the 1935 earthquake memorial service.
subfiles.summary: Memo finds Neville's $10.17 memorial wreath for 1923 earthquake victims appropriate for reimbursement, since other missions sent wreaths.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1461: Memorial services for victims of the 1923 earthquake
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. chargé d’affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports foreign diplomatic participation in the September 1, 1935 memorial services in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 1461: foreign representatives were formally included and 224 foreign victims enshrined in Shinto and Buddhist ceremonies at Honjo, arranged by Dr. Issa Tanimura; Neville requests wreath reimbursement.

subfiles.title: Tanimura letter thanking the American Embassy for its floral tribute
subfiles.to: Edward S. Crocker, Second Secretary, American Embassy
subfiles.about: Thanks the American government and Crocker for participating in the earthquake memorial ceremonies.
subfiles.summary: Tanimura thanks the American Embassy for its floral tribute to the 1923 victims and Crocker for attending both ceremonies.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Foreign Relations of the United States, 1923
subfiles.about: Points to correspondence concerning permission to publish records from file 894.48B.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: permission to publish earthquake correspondence from file 894.48B in Foreign Relations of the United States, 1923 (file 026/1080).

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for a publication instruction to Japan
subfiles.about: Points to an instruction seeking Japanese permission to publish correspondence from the earthquake file.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Instruction 1130 to Japan on permission to publish selected 894.48B correspondence in Foreign Relations, 1923 (026/1094).

subfiles.title: File jacket: Visit of Japan’s People’s Envoys of Gratitude
subfiles.about: Identifies the case file devoted to the 1930 visit of Japan’s People’s Envoys of Gratitude.
subfiles.summary: File jacket for the visit of Japan's People's Envoys of Gratitude to the US.

subfiles.title: Largely illegible handwritten filing note
subfiles.about: Contains fragmentary handwritten remarks apparently concerning whether an activity was official or unofficial.
subfiles.summary: Largely illegible handwritten filing note mentioning something official or unofficial.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 19 on American kindness and prospective gratitude envoys
subfiles.from: William R. Castle Jr., U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a Jiji Shimpo editorial and reports plans to send young Japanese women to thank the United States.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 19: Castle notes a Japanese newspaper recalled American earthquake aid during the London Naval Conference; young women will tour American cities on the President Pierce under Hidesaburo Yokoyama.

subfiles.title: American Kindness Recalled
subfiles.about: Reviews American relief after the 1923 earthquake and announces plans for a mission of thanks.
subfiles.summary: The editorial recounts American diplomatic, naval, military, medical, Red Cross, financial, and private relief after the destruction of Tokyo and Yokohama. It praises Cyrus E. Woods, the Asiatic Squadron, President Coolidge, and the American public, and cites the commemorative hospital at Honjo as a permanent symbol of goodwill. It announces the Jiji Shimpo’s plan to send Japanese women to the United States to express national gratitude.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 40 on the Envoys of Gratitude
subfiles.from: William R. Castle Jr., U.S. Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the envoys’ forthcoming tour and asks whether Mrs. Caldwell can accompany them.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 40: four young women arrive in San Francisco April 2 as Envoys of Gratitude; Castle asks whether Mrs. Caldwell can accompany them at Shidehara's request.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 44 identifying the four envoys
subfiles.from: William R. Castle Jr., U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.about: Lists the four selected envoys and summarizes their education and family backgrounds.
subfiles.summary: Castle identifies Kimi Ashino, Yoshiko Matsudaira, Yoshiko Sato, and Sumiko Tokuda as the selected envoys. He supplies biographical details and reports that Toshiko Matsudaira and Hidesaburo Yokoyama will accompany them. The party is scheduled to reach San Francisco on April 2 aboard the President Pierce.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 50 approving Mrs. Caldwell’s participation
subfiles.about: Offers Mrs. Caldwell as the envoys’ escort after their arrival in Washington and reports requests for entry courtesies.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 50: Mrs. Caldwell can meet the envoys in Washington and accompany them thereafter; Treasury and Labor were notified and customs facilities requested.

subfiles.title: Request to facilitate the envoys’ admission at San Francisco
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests immigration assistance for the envoys and their escorts upon arrival.
subfiles.summary: White asks the Labor Department to instruct the Commissioner of Immigration at San Francisco to expedite the party’s landing. He explains the mission’s purpose, Jiji Shimpo sponsorship, and the distinguished character of the selection committee and envoys.

subfiles.title: Request for customs courtesies for the envoys
subfiles.about: Requests customs courtesies and free-entry privileges for the envoys and their escorts.
subfiles.summary: The Department designates the Japanese party as distinguished foreign visitors and asks that customs officials facilitate their arrival in San Francisco. The letter explains that the mission will thank Americans for relief after the great earthquake and notes the prominence of its Japanese sponsors.

subfiles.title: Jiji Shimpo announcement of the gratitude mission
subfiles.about: Announces the planned mission and requests American cooperation and publicity.
subfiles.summary: Jiji Shimpo announces women envoys will thank Americans and report Tokyo and Yokohama's reconstruction, with a provisional itinerary including Hoover, Coolidge, Cyrus Woods and the Red Cross; asks American support.

subfiles.title: Brief outline of the original plan for People’s Envoys of Gratitude
subfiles.about: Sets out the purpose, mission, selection process, qualifications, and proposed timing of the envoy project.
subfiles.summary: Outline of the original plan to send Japanese women to thank the US and present reconstruction photographs, with selection committee and qualifications, leaving before March 26 and returning in May.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Rebuilt
subfiles.from: Japan Advertiser, translating a Jiji Shimpo editorial
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo’s reconstruction and the scale of American relief following the earthquake.
subfiles.summary: Clipping 'Tokyo Rebuilt' recounts American diplomatic, naval, medical, Red Cross and financial aid after 1923, praising Cyrus Woods and the Honjo hospital, as completed reconstruction renews Japanese gratitude.

subfiles.title: Treasury Department approval of customs courtesies
subfiles.from: Seymour Lowman, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Confirms authorization of customs courtesies and free-entry privileges for the envoys.
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Lowman confirms the San Francisco Collector of Customs will extend customary privileges to the four women and their chaperon or escort.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 49 accepting the Caldwell arrangement
subfiles.from: William R. Castle Jr., U.S. Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Baron Shidehara’s acceptance of the plan for Mrs. Caldwell to assist the envoys.
subfiles.summary: Castle says the Caldwell arrangement is acceptable to Baron Shidehara.

subfiles.title: Labor Department approval of immigration assistance
subfiles.from: Robe Carl White, Assistant Secretary of Labor
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that immigration officials will facilitate the envoys’ admission to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Labor Department says the San Francisco immigration commissioner will extend every courtesy and expedite the Japanese party's admission from the President Pierce.

subfiles.title: Jiji Shimpo letter announcing the four selected envoys
subfiles.from: Takuzo Itakura and Nisaburo Momiyama, Jiji Shimpo
subfiles.about: Names the selected envoys and asks for American assistance with their unprecedented mission.
subfiles.summary: Jiji Shimpo names envoys Ashino, Sato, Tokuda and Matsudaira, lists the selection committee, explains the increase from two to four, and asks cooperation.

subfiles.title: Biographies of the four Envoys of Gratitude
subfiles.about: Provides ages, education, family connections, and accomplishments of the four envoys.
subfiles.summary: Biographies of Kimi Ashino, Sumiko Tokuda, Yoshiko Sato and Yoshiko Matsudaira: education, family, English study, diplomatic and aristocratic ties, and Tokuda's Lincoln Essay Prize.

subfiles.title: Revised brief outline of the four-envoy plan
subfiles.about: Revises the mission plan to provide for four envoys and adds further prospective hosts.
subfiles.summary: Revised outline: envoys thank Americans and report reconstruction, calling on Hoover, Coolidge, Woods, the Red Cross, Salvation Army and officials; lists the expanded committee and qualifications.

subfiles.title: Itinerary for the People’s Envoys of Gratitude
subfiles.about: Gives the proposed March–June trans-Pacific and American travel schedule.
subfiles.summary: Itinerary from Yokohama through Honolulu and nine mainland cities and back, with dates, trains, ships, hotels and connections.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Jiji Shimpo letter announcing the four envoys
subfiles.from: Takuzo Itakura and Nisaburo Momiyama, Jiji Shimpo
subfiles.about: Duplicates the announcement naming the four envoys and requesting cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate Jiji Shimpo letter naming the four envoys and committee and explaining the expansion from two to four.

subfiles.title: Duplicate biographies of the four envoys
subfiles.about: Duplicates the profiles of Ashino, Tokuda, Sato, and Matsudaira.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate biographies of the four envoys as educated representatives of modern Japanese womanhood.

subfiles.title: Duplicate revised outline of the four-envoy plan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the revised statement of the mission’s purpose and organization.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate revised outline of the four-envoy gratitude mission.

subfiles.title: Duplicate itinerary for the People’s Envoys of Gratitude
subfiles.about: Duplicates the trans-Pacific and American itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate itinerary from Yokohama to Honolulu, across the US and back.

subfiles.title: Coolidge letter offering assistance with the envoys’ visit
subfiles.about: Offers to receive or otherwise assist the envoys if their visit is coordinated officially.
subfiles.summary: Coolidge forwards a communication and offers help through the Japanese Embassy and State Department, asking what would aid the administration and Japan.

subfiles.title: Jiji Shimpo request for a meeting with Calvin Coolidge
subfiles.from: Takuzo Itakura and Nisaburo Momiyama, Jiji Shimpo
subfiles.about: Requests that the four envoys be permitted to thank Coolidge personally for his 1923 relief leadership.
subfiles.summary: Jiji Shimpo asks Coolidge to receive the four envoys at Northampton to thank him for earthquake aid during his presidency; outline and photographs enclosed.

subfiles.title: Jiji Shimpo circular naming the selected envoys
subfiles.from: Takuzo Itakura and Nisaburo Momiyama, Jiji Shimpo
subfiles.about: Provides the envoy names, selection committee, and request for assistance.
subfiles.summary: Jiji Shimpo circular names the four selected women, lists the selection committee and explains the enlargement of the mission.

subfiles.title: Biographical enclosure on the four envoys
subfiles.about: Supplies biographical information about the four original envoys.
subfiles.summary: Biographical enclosure on Ashino, Tokuda, Sato and Matsudaira, with ties to Japanese diplomats and Princess Chichibu.

subfiles.title: Mission-plan enclosure for the four envoys
subfiles.about: Outlines the purpose, activities, selection, and qualifications of the gratitude mission.
subfiles.summary: Mission-plan enclosure: the women will thank American relief providers and present materials on reconstructed Tokyo and Yokohama; recipients, committee and qualifications named.

subfiles.title: Individuals and organizations to be visited by the Envoys of Gratitude
subfiles.about: Lists proposed official, charitable, press, diplomatic, and civic calls in each city.
subfiles.summary: List of visits by city from Honolulu to Portland, including Hoover, John Barton Payne, Cyrus Woods, Roland Morris, Cardinal Hayes and Coolidge, newspapers, civic bodies and relief groups.

subfiles.title: Itinerary enclosure for the envoys’ tour
subfiles.about: Provides detailed transportation and lodging plans for the envoys’ American tour.
subfiles.summary: Itinerary enclosure: departure from Yokohama March 18, return June 2, with cities, times, trains, ships and hotels.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Coolidge concerning the envoys
subfiles.about: Welcomes Coolidge’s willingness to receive the envoys and promises to notify him of their Northampton schedule.
subfiles.summary: State tells Coolidge the unofficial mission merits assistance given Japanese official support, and his reception of the women will benefit US-Japan relations.

subfiles.title: Identification sheet for four envoys
subfiles.about: Lists four envoy names in English with accompanying Japanese characters.
subfiles.summary: Identification sheet for envoys Yoshiko Sato, Sumiko Tokuda, Yoshiko Matsudaira and Kimi Ashino, likely a photo caption.

subfiles.title: Coolidge letter arranging an April 25 reception
subfiles.about: Agrees that Calvin and Grace Coolidge will receive the four envoys on April 25.
subfiles.summary: Coolidge and Mrs. Coolidge agree to receive the four Japanese women on April 25, if acceptable to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note requesting a reception by Mrs. Hoover
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Asks whether Mrs. Hoover will receive the five women envoys and Madame Debuchi.
subfiles.summary: Debuchi identifies five women sent under Jiji Shimpo sponsorship, including the newly listed Keiko Nakamura. He notes their expected April 14 arrival in Washington and asks the Department to arrange a call on Mrs. Hoover, accompanied by Madame Debuchi.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note requesting a presidential reception
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests that President Hoover receive the five envoys and their accompanying party.
subfiles.summary: The note again lists the five women and explains their mission of gratitude. It adds Toshiko Matsudaira and Hidesaburo Yokoyama to the party and asks whether President Hoover will receive them during their Washington stay.

subfiles.title: White House acceptance of the presidential reception
subfiles.from: George Akerson, Secretary to the President
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that President Hoover will receive the ambassador and the Japanese party on April 15.
subfiles.summary: Akerson says the President will receive the ambassador and young Japanese women at 12:30 p.m. on April 15; Mrs. Hoover will probably receive them separately.

subfiles.title: Acceptance of Mrs. Hoover’s reception
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that Mrs. Hoover will receive the envoys and their chaperons on April 17.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Hoover will receive Madame Debuchi and the five envoys at 4 p.m. on April 17, with Toshiko Matsudaira and Mrs. Caldwell invited.

subfiles.title: Cotton letter requesting White House appointments
subfiles.from: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: George Akerson, Secretary to the President
subfiles.about: Explains the mission and formally requests presidential and First Lady receptions.
subfiles.summary: Cotton gives names, dates, committee and unofficial status of the five-woman delegation, asks that the Ambassador present them to Hoover without photography, and asks if Mrs. Hoover can receive them.

subfiles.title: State Department note confirming Mrs. Hoover’s reception
subfiles.about: Confirms the April 17 appointment with Mrs. Hoover.
subfiles.summary: State note tells Debuchi Mrs. Hoover will receive Madame Debuchi and the five envoys, with Toshiko Matsudaira and Mrs. Caldwell also attending.

subfiles.title: State Department note confirming President Hoover’s reception
subfiles.from: Francis White for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Confirms the April 15 presidential appointment for the envoys and accompanying representatives.
subfiles.summary: State note tells Debuchi President Hoover will receive the five envoys at the Executive Office at 12:30 p.m., with Toshiko Matsudaira and Hidesaburo Yokoyama.

subfiles.title: American Red Cross assessment of the envoys’ visit
subfiles.from: John Barton Payne, Chairman, American Red Cross
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Thanks Cotton for background material and reports that the envoys’ Red Cross visit was successful.
subfiles.summary: Payne says the envoys' visit to American Red Cross headquarters was a great success.

subfiles.title: White House transmittal of messages left by the Goodwill Mission
subfiles.from: Lawrence Richey, Secretary to the President
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards letters presented to President Hoover by the Japanese Goodwill Mission.
subfiles.summary: Richey sends Cotton the Japanese messages of gratitude for American earthquake relief that the mission left with President Hoover.

subfiles.title: Nakagawa message on completion of reconstruction
subfiles.from: Nozomu Nakagawa, Director of the Reconstruction Bureau
subfiles.about: Thanks the United States for assistance that helped make the reconstruction of Tokyo and Yokohama possible.
subfiles.summary: Nakagawa recalls the destruction, says American sympathy and material help lightened Japan's burden, asks the envoys to report the results, and thanks the American government and people for the Reconstruction Bureau.

subfiles.title: Jiji Shimpo message to the President of the United States
subfiles.from: Ikunoshin Kadono for the Jiji Shimpo
subfiles.about: Presents the five envoys and messages of gratitude to the President.
subfiles.summary: Jiji Shimpo message says Tokyo and Yokohama citizens thank the President and Americans for 1923 relief, identifies the five envoys and committee, and mentions a reconstruction photograph volume.

subfiles.title: Mayor Horikiri’s message of thanks to the American people
subfiles.about: Uses the Goodwill Mission to convey Tokyo’s thanks and report the completion of reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Mayor Horikiri thanks Americans for their generosity six and a half years earlier, points to a booklet on Tokyo's reconstruction, and hopes the mission deepens friendship.

subfiles.title: Instruction to acknowledge three messages presented to President Hoover
subfiles.about: Directs the ambassador to acknowledge letters from Horikiri, Nakagawa, and Kadono on the President’s behalf.
subfiles.summary: Instruction transmits three messages of thanks left with President Hoover and asks suitable acknowledgments.

subfiles.title: Instruction transmitting messages presented at the State Department
subfiles.about: Sends two Japanese messages for acknowledgment and a press release on Tokyo’s reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Instruction forwards messages from Tokyo's mayor and the Reconstruction Bureau director presented April 15, with an April 2 press release of the Debuchi-Cotton exchange of notes.

subfiles.title: Copy of Nakagawa’s reconstruction message
subfiles.from: Nozomu Nakagawa, Director of the Reconstruction Bureau
subfiles.about: Repeats Nakagawa’s formal thanks for American assistance with post-earthquake reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Copy of Nakagawa's message on the completion of reconstruction, thanking Americans, a printed form letter.

subfiles.title: Copy of Mayor Horikiri’s message
subfiles.about: Repeats Tokyo’s formal appreciation for American relief and reports completion of the capital’s reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Horikiri asks the Jiji Shimpo Goodwill Mission to thank the American people for their generosity after the 1923 catastrophe. He refers recipients to the Tokyo Reconstruction Work booklet and hopes the mission will strengthen friendship and cooperation. A file note states that the communication was a printed form letter.
